mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals labor market deterioration that precedes economic slowdowns, causing investors to reduce equity exposure and generate negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand that drives corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery phase where industrial production (INDPRO) declines for two consecutive months and then rises, it signals manufacturing sector strengthening that boosts corporate profits and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 2 consecutive months then rises
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates labor market strength that supports consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS grows, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When core inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase where quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 1.5% but shows slowing momentum, it signals an economic peak that triggers profit-taking and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods in the late-cycle regime, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates monetary tightening amid labor market strength, reducing corporate investment and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.
